headline: High-risk shared-state orchestration: LangGraph can write shared checkpointer state while nuwa-skill has allowlisted egress, creating leakage and conflict pathways; prompt-injection risk is lower but present via shared outputs.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LangGraph can expose outputs through application-defined files, stdin/stdout, and developer-wired nodes, while nuwa-skill is a separate open-source agent with network egress. The pair lacks a documented isolation boundary, so if LangGraph outputs are fed into nuwa-skill or a shared workspace, instruction-hijacking is plausible. Uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF LangGraph node outputs are copied into nuwa-skill prompts or files
IF both agents share a workspace or message queue without provenance tags
mitigations: Add a strict delimiter and provenance header to all inter-agent messages
Disable automatic ingestion of raw file contents into prompts
Route shared artifacts through a review-only queue
requires-engineering: add content provenance tracking between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: LangGraph explicitly handles model provider API keys and can read/write application-defined files; its shared checkpointer store can persist graph state across instances. nuwa-skill has allowlisted network egress, so if sensitive graph state reaches it, leakage can occur through its outbound calls. The pairwise path is inferred, but the shared-state plus egress combination is enough for medium.
conditions: IF sensitive graph state is stored in the shared checkpointer
IF nuwa-skill receives that state and transmits it via outbound requests
mitigations: Keep secrets out of shared graph state
Store per-agent state in separate namespaces
Review outbound destinations for nuwa-skill
Rotate any exposed API keys immediately
requires-engineering: encrypt checkpointer contents at rest

C_capability_conflict.rationale: LangGraph can write application-defined files and uses a shared checkpointer store across instances; nuwa-skill has network egress but no documented locking or coordination. Even without explicit git or filesystem overlap in nuwa-skill, shared mutable state can still race or overwrite between agents. Because the exact shared resource is not documented, uncertainty escalates to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same checkpointer namespace or workspace
IF one agent updates shared state without a lock or version check
mitigations: Assign separate storage namespaces per agent
Add optimistic concurrency checks on shared records
Serialize writes through a single coordinator
requires-engineering: introduce distributed locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: LangGraph is a low-level orchestration framework where developer-wired nodes can pass outputs downstream, and nuwa-skill is a separate research agent that may act on received inputs. If LangGraph-produced facts are treated as authoritative by nuwa-skill, errors can cascade into later actions. The interaction is not directly documented, so I choose medium over low due to plausible default orchestration patterns.
conditions: IF LangGraph outputs are forwarded into nuwa-skill without verification
IF nuwa-skill uses those outputs to generate further actions or reports
mitigations: Insert a verification step before forwarding outputs
Require citations or source links for all forwarded claims
Flag low-confidence outputs for human review
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks

E_compliance.rationale: LangGraph touches application-defined graph state and model-provider API keys, while nuwa-skill has no documented residency, retention, or certification details. No concrete compliance mismatch is evidenced, but the absence of documented controls on the second agent means a narrow compliance gap is plausible if regulated data enters the pair. I cite only agent_a because agent_b lacks relevant compliance fields.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into LangGraph graph state
IF nuwa-skill processes that same regulated data under undocumented retention or residency rules
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in shared state
Document retention and deletion rules for both agents
Restrict nuwa-skill to non-sensitive datasets
requires-engineering: perform a compliance review of nuwa-skill
